project.purpose: Decompose confirmed website Human/Agent authority and effect-replay responsibilities, with explicit canary scope and cross-Security consumer contracts. No new Web runtime or registry.

nodes.label: WebAuthnPrincipalAndChallenge
nodes.responsibility: Bind one account/Principal to an authenticated WebAuthn credential/challenge lifecycle by delegating protocol verification to SimpleWebAuthn.
nodes.authority: Web product/session/effect state only; Security/provider cryptographic and policy truth remain external
inputs: principal/enrollment context; one-shot challenge and credential records
outputs: authenticated Principal identity and consumed challenge or denial
nodes.behavioralContract: Challenge consumption is one-shot; credential and challenge are persisted to the Owner-local store; browser/virtual authenticator proof is not a claim of physical human presence.
acceptance: Native Challenge consumer reuses one owner transaction kernel; exact one-shot state, purpose and expiry semantics are unchanged under deterministic acknowledgement and writer contention faults.
Owner session/challenge tests verify one-shot behavior and browser E2E evidence scopes without treating canary enrollment as production-ready.

Native ChallengeStore consumer tests prove payload snapshot capture, digest mismatch/malformed JSON rejection before consume, rollback and one-shot behavior; no arbitrary DB tamper resistance is claimed.
mustNotOwn: Security Agent OAuth/DPoP verification or Agent admission policy
production IAM enrollment or deployment acceptance
formalObligations: Refinement gap: real external authenticator/canary enrollment/production recovery and installed TLS context remain UNKNOWN.

nodes.label: BrowserSessionAndMutationAdmission
nodes.responsibility: Admit human browser state mutations only under an authenticated opaque session plus CSRF, exact Origin and Fetch-Metadata checks.
nodes.authority: Web product/session/effect state only; Security/provider cryptographic and policy truth remain external
inputs: opaque browser session cookie; server-stored hash, session expiry/revocation state
outputs: Principal session projection; admitted authenticated mutation or typed denial
nodes.behavioralContract: Session token is not an authority-bearing credential beyond its exact server-bound identity; unsafe browser mutations require same-site and CSRF guards; session idle/absolute expiry, revocation and audit operate independently of Agent DPoP flow.
acceptance: Native web tests verify hashed session tokens, absent-origin/CSRF denial, idle expiration and session revocation.
mustNotOwn: Security Agent OAuth/DPoP verification or Agent admission policy
production IAM enrollment or deployment acceptance
formalObligations: A local test-only SQLite-backed session is not evidence of production reliability, or an argument to retain SQLite in long-term persistent architecture.

nodes.label: AgentGrantIssueAndRevocation
nodes.responsibility: Manage Principal-owned delegated Agent Grants, scope, revocation and remaining-effect budgets without inventing OAuth/DPoP verifier or Security policy.
nodes.authority: Web product/session/effect state only; Security/provider cryptographic and policy truth remain external
inputs: WebAuthn-authenticated Principal authorization and grant request
Agent identity, audience, actions, risk and resource scope
outputs: versioned Grant record; revocation and remaining-quota state with consumer-visible standing
nodes.behavioralContract: Issued Grants and revocations bind one Principal/Agent/scope and remain source-owned; revoked Grants block future effects without invalidating already committed historical exact replay.
acceptance: Opt-in Solid 2 actual operator route consumes the same authenticated Owner observation and exact displayed fields, never an admission decision. The explicit generation/lifecycle fence clears private observations and rejects late success; the native select is read-only. No test bridge in product build; absent/invalid configured assets fail startup.
Owner Agent authority tests cover Grant revocation and future-effect denial distinct from historical committed receipts.
mustNotOwn: Security Agent OAuth/DPoP verification or Agent admission policy
production IAM enrollment or deployment acceptance
formalObligations: No generalization from canary Grant scope to live provider IAM or production issuance recovery.

nodes.label: SecurityOwnedAgentAdmissionAdapter
nodes.responsibility: Consume exact Web-local Grant/effect context and delegate Agent request verification plus Agent/Effect Admission to existing Security-owned contracts; produce scoped decision without owning Security cryptography, Rego or executable effects.
nodes.authority: Web product/session/effect state only; Security/provider cryptographic and policy truth remain external
inputs: Agent method/origin and OAuth/DPoP evidence; Web-local replay guard
typed exact Grant, effect, risk and optional approval inputs
outputs: typed VerifiedAgent plus Security admission-chain decision or fail-closed rejection
nodes.behavioralContract: If Security verifier is absent or returns an invalid decision, admission fails closed. OAuth/DPoP verification and policy are consumed from Security-owned contracts; Web retains only local DPoP replay state and request-to-policy input binding.
acceptance: Native DPoP local replay persistence reuses the same owner transaction kernel; expiry cleanup, replay denial and insertion share the original atomic boundary, with no change to Security verification or admission.
Existing Web tests exercise missing Security verifier rejection and Security verifier boundary; real installation qualification remains UNKNOWN.
mustNotOwn: Security Agent OAuth/DPoP verification or Agent admission policy
production IAM enrollment or deployment acceptance
formalObligations: Cross-Owner psi=>phi and deployed DPoP proof currentness UNKNOWN; Web does not mint Security policy authority.

nodes.label: EffectBoundStepUpAndReplay
nodes.responsibility: Commit exactly scoped canary create/publish mutations under independently admitted Grant/Agent/Effect policy and effect-bound WebAuthn step-up while preserving exact historical replay.
inputs: exact effect digest and receipt identity
R4 effect-specific WebAuthn step-up approval when required
outputs: new committed canary receipt, identical historical replay, or explicit conflict/deny
nodes.behavioralContract: R2 create commits under admitted scope; R4 publish requires step-up approval bound to the exact effect and consumes it once; committed approval evidence cannot be reopened and pending approval lookup excludes committed effects; identical replay preserves previous receipt and conflicting payloads or fresh revoked-grant effects reject.
acceptance: R15 bounded native concurrent histories: response and exact independent final facts admit a real-time-respecting sequential witness; native unique-key races and forced snapshot interleaving, isolation/checker negative controls; no claim about unknown outcomes or full interleavings.

R14 native target qualification: full Rust discovery and fresh Nextest JUnit exact identities, no omitted tests/retries, independent generated Note/Audit model with stable shrunk regressions, verified PG fixture cleanup; explicit target owner verification, root CI integration separate.

R13 native Rust PG candidate uses a bounded mature pool, affirmative terminality before recycle, caller-held prepared Note/Audit identities and coherent read-only observation; actual post-COMMIT future cancellation and wire ACK loss recover exact evidence without retry. Full schema, authenticated composition and single-writer cutover remain gated.

Rust async PG Note/Audit source candidate: same actual SQLite projection, exact writes and final readback after deferred constraints, explicit rollback, native cancellation and real COMMIT ACK loss UNKNOWN; full schema/pool/HTTP/single-writer migration remain separate gates.

Human canary draft creation also uses the shared native owner transaction kernel, requires exact Note and Audit cardinality and final projection before commit; no partial write, automatic retry, or shared authorization decision. Stable list order is created_at DESC, note_id ASC; principal-local composite and nonunique partial audit indexes preserve existing rows on reopen.

Effect, Challenge and DPoP share one native BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK implementation; domain error codes remain distinct, uncertain connections are quarantined, and no automatic retry follows ambiguous outcomes.
Native Web tests cover exact replay/conflict, R4 approval and revoked Grant historical replay.
Local canary write != external provider effect, no installed/exactly-once distributed claim.
Native HTTP tests replay three deterministic async admission interleavings; bounded TLA+ model checks response invariants, not deployed refinement.

Native SQLite tests preserve exact target Note, Grant, Receipt, Audit and Approval postconditions or roll back; audit lookup uses a bounded non-unique partial index, preserving duplicates for detection.
WebStore is a compatibility facade; one AgentEffectStore owns the transaction, with receipt and approval components on the same connection. No new database or authority.

Native contention with a peer WAL writer returns typed 503 only for BUSY before transaction acquisition. Historical replay needs no writer lock; after acquisition preserve original error and reconcile by identity without automatic retry.

Native owner transaction recovery covers BEGIN/COMMIT acknowledgement faults, rollback failure and explicit connection reopening, and abrupt disposable child process death on both sides of COMMIT. A bounded trace oracle checks identity, quota, revision and receipt on every transition; no automatic Effect retry.

An initial receipt miss is provisional until native writer admission; a second lookup resolves exact historical replay or conflicting identity before mutable Grant checks. A COMMIT exception does not establish non-commit; rollback only while the connection reports an active transaction and never automatically reissue.

Deterministic two-connection WAL tests cover create/publish exact replay, conflict, stale distinct effects, and before/after-commit acknowledgement injection; no process-crash, lock-wait or distributed delivery proof.
formalObligations: PG candidate primitive witness only: acquire transaction-scoped effect identity lock before Grant row lock, re-observe receipt in a fresh READ COMMITTED statement, preserve revision CAS and exact serialized receipt bytes. A failed lock or unknown commit is not evidence of non-commit; no automatic reissue. Hash collisions can conservatively deny disjoint work. Full schema, async driver, approval/note row lock order, error mapping and migration remain unqualified.

A failed rollback quarantines the owner connection before close; normal facade and transaction operations reject without observing tentative state even if native close fails. A new usable connection and explicit observation are required; raw native instrumentation is not an isolation boundary.
Source/transaction behavior does not prove installed WebStore durability, physical provider effects or cross-provider exactly-once.
nodes.authority: Web canary identity/grant/receipt source only, not external provider or Security truth
mustNotOwn: production publication or installed provider effect
